task: Find a specialist or retrieval system that reduces omitted skill alternatives and improves evidence-backed combinations without requiring the user to name candidates.

explicit: User expects relevant skills to be considered proactively
Repo is intended to retain research, compare current versions and installed skills, and improve recommendations
constraints.scope: Research and a targeted advisor-instruction improvement; no candidate installation, new background service or model download.
constraints.prior_preferences: Keep existing installation gates and prior selections/exclusions; interest in specialist agents does not authorize bulk installation.

diagnosis.observed: The first recommendation concentrated on the 3D implementation stack and deferred broad design tools collectively. The user had to name UI/UX Pro Max, Taste, Emil and Apple Design to get a substantive comparison.
diagnosis.distinction: This was incomplete coverage/explanation, not proof that all four should have been selected. Relevant catalog entries and routing guidance already existed.
diagnosis.retrieval_limit: scripts/knowledge.py search uses token intersections with name bonuses and a result limit. It is not semantic routing, a compatibility engine or a mandatory capability-coverage check.
diagnosis.system_limit: A senior-expert persona changes instructions; it does not itself provide persistent memory, fresh upstream discovery or objectively better judgments.

candidates.review_depth: Read saved and current SKILL.md and compared their complete strings (identical); read current src/find.ts and existing audit/inventory. CLI not executed.
candidates.fit: Useful existing discovery layer for finding candidates through skills.sh. Reuse the saved option subject to device readiness; no new discovery persona is necessary.
candidates.overlap: Overlaps the repo's research search but reaches an external registry. Does not replace task-specific source evaluation or conflict analysis.
prerequisites: Network access to public skills.sh search
Node/npm only if using an inspected pinned CLI
candidates.costs: No API key required for public discovery according to saved review; ordinary model/network usage. CLI implementation sends search requests and invokes telemetry.
uncertainties: Current CLI sorts returned candidates by install count; the SKILL.md relies heavily on installs/stars for quality screening. Popularity is a discovery signal, not proof of fit or quality.
Noninteractive query prints candidates; interactive selection can enter installation. Do not treat every find invocation as mutation-free.
Saved payload existence and historical Mac installation do not establish the current laptop state.

candidates.review_depth: Read full current Tool Evaluator, Agents Orchestrator and Codex integration instructions; inspected current tree and recent open-item titles. No converters/installers or embedded code executed.
candidates.fit: Tool Evaluator is the closest specialist role: requirements, alternatives, realistic trials, cost/integration and documented recommendations. Orchestrator coordinates implementation and QA when that separate job is needed.
candidates.overlap: Tool Evaluator's methodology overlaps ADVISOR.md; adapt only missing evaluation duties. Full Orchestrator overlaps existing engineering workflows and does not discover current skills by itself.
prerequisites: Underlying capable model and permitted tools
Actual candidate evidence and representative trials
Codex host support if using converted custom agents
candidates.costs: MIT according to historical source review; role prompts consume the host's normal model quota. Multi-agent use adds calls/latency. Current full payload licensing/security not re-audited.
uncertainties: Role statements about experience and memory are prompt instructions, not credentials or a storage implementation.
Embedded scoring example calls undefined test methods and includes generic weights; it is not a ready-made autonomous tool benchmark.
Enterprise ROI/vendor-negotiation sections are excessive for a small skill comparison.
Current installer PRs include symlink and Python isolation fixes; titles inspected only, no claim of verified vulnerabilities or fixes.

candidates.review_depth: Read full listed files, current tree, issue #11 and open PR #7. No dependencies/models installed and no evaluation executed.
candidates.fit: Closest technical research component for retrieving relevant skills from a large overlapping pool, then reranking with instruction-body content.
candidates.overlap: Potential alternative to lexical candidate retrieval. Still needs a maintained source index, per-capability query planning, exact upstream/device verification, conflict selection and outcome evaluation.
prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, transformers and model weights
An indexed skill corpus with source/body metadata
Hardware and latency validation; README assumes CUDA, code has a CPU fallback
Separate model/data license and remote-code review
candidates.costs: Code README declares MIT; model weights and datasets have separate terms. Local inference consumes memory/compute; no benchmark performed on the user's hardware.
uncertainties: Public default branch is primarily an evaluation release, not a complete drop-in Codex advisor.
MCP integration is open PR #7, unmerged at the check time. Do not describe it as shipped.
README reports 74% average Hit@1 on 75 scored tasks; these are maintainer benchmark claims, not this task's measured accuracy. Open issue #11 reports reproduction disparity, unverified here.
Body-aware does not mean every instruction is read: evaluated retrieval uses body_max=8000 characters, default rerank formatting truncates body to 2000, token maximum defaults to 4096.
Model loaders use trust_remote_code=True and dependencies are broadly specified; these require review before execution.
Retrieval relevance does not establish compatibility, safety, superior output or an optimal multi-skill combination.

candidates.identity: OpenViking context database and optional Codex memory integration
candidates.review_depth: Read core README architecture/prerequisite sections, full retrieval specification and initial Codex integration/hook sections. Did not audit server, plugin hooks or full reference corpus.
candidates.fit: Potential future storage/retrieval layer for documents, skills and decision memory; supports scoped semantic retrieval and optional session-intent query planning.
candidates.overlap: Overlaps the repo's persistent knowledge and lookup. Much heavier than a targeted candidate-coverage instruction fix.
prerequisites: Python/uv and embedding plus language/vision model configuration per README
Client/plugin support for optional lifecycle integration
candidates.costs: Current README declares AGPLv3; hosting, embeddings and model calls have operational costs. Detailed licensing/deployment review remains separate.
uncertainties: Codex example captures conversation turns into the configured server and recalls context via hooks; it is not simply an index over sanitized repo files. Do not adopt default capture silently.
Current retrieval documentation describes global vector recall and optional reranking of abstracts, not automatic recursive directory navigation.
Memory retrieval does not guarantee exhaustive candidate selection or keep upstream repositories current automatically.
Maintainer benchmark claims were not reproduced; recent issue titles were checked only.

decision.status: Source-based recommendations and a procedural correction; not a proven automated router.
decision.recommendation: Keep the repo as the evidence/decision base. Require job decomposition, separate discovery per capability, explicit coverage of credible known alternatives and conflict review. Trial a narrowly adapted Tool Evaluator role only if it adds measurable value; evaluate SkillRouter if semantic retrieval remains a demonstrated bottleneck.

inputs: design 3d animation motion website scroll effects realistic model view
evidence.method: scripts/knowledge.py search, limit 10, unmodified current index
evidence.result: Broad query returned prior decisions and motion-heavy entries, without standalone UI/UX Pro Max, Taste, Emil or Apple entries. Design query surfaced UI/UX Pro Max; gesture query surfaced Apple and Emil. Current index includes the earlier decisions, so this is not a historical replay or an accuracy benchmark.

evidence.input: Original book/page-scroll/shirt-inspection brief without skill names
evidence.criteria: Account for visual direction, assets, rendering, scroll, gesture interaction and verification; address relevant catalog alternatives without selecting them all.
evidence.result: Amended instructions require the missing discovery/coverage steps. Earlier source comparison supplies concrete reasons for selecting/defering named alternatives. Self-review only; no independent agent outcome test.

evidence.criteria: Answer the simple concept question without broad discovery or installing a framework.
evidence.result: New requirement is scoped to recommendations spanning several capabilities; the concept question does not trigger it. No model benchmark run.

unperformed_checks: Performance/quality benchmark of SkillRouter, OpenViking or specialist personas

feedback.text: User questions whether relevant alternatives will be missed unless they name them and asks for a specialist/expert agent or GitHub system to address this.
A recommendation should expose enough candidate coverage to be auditable; user did not ask to activate all candidates or install a multi-agent framework.

future_evaluation.positive_case: Reuse the book/shirt prompt without tool names. Require coverage of all necessary capabilities and explicit treatment of relevant known alternatives, allowing justified deferral.
future_evaluation.edge_case: A simple conceptual question or isolated nonvisual bug should not cause broad design discovery or bulk skill loading.
future_evaluation.status: Proposed evaluation; only manual walkthrough and lexical query observations completed.
